results.q: How much does Norfolk budget for tree care?
results.answer:
I found no budget line that is only for tree care. Trees sit inside a larger unit, Park and Forestry Operations, which also covers mowing, landscaping, litter control and athletic fields. So the figures below are for the whole unit, not trees alone.

**Park and Forestry Operations** (from the City's financial system, under Parks & Recreation):
- **FY2025:** budget $11,728,050. Actual spending was $11,536,917 (98.4%).
- **FY2026:** budget $12,661,811. Actual spending was $12,169,859 (96.1%).
- **FY2027 (in progress):** budget $13,139,514. Spending so far is $4,562,793 (34.7%), with about 38.9% of the year elapsed on 2026-11-20.

The FY2026 adopted budget book lists the same program at $12,661,811 and 128.0 FTE. It marks demand as "Does Not Meet Demand." The FY2027 book lists 2 Tree Trimmer I and 3 Tree Trimmer II positions in Parks and Recreation.

**Tree-specific pieces I found in the budget books:**
- The Siren case file cites the FY2024 adopted budget as showing a $250,000 adjustment for the tree care maintenance contract. That contract is used to remove decaying or diseased trees.
- It cites the FY2025 adopted budget as adding $400,000 for tree maintenance to reduce a backlog the City attributes to the pandemic. My search excerpt of that section showed only a $412,544 landscaping item, so I haven't confirmed the $400,000 line myself.
- The case file says a Forestry Supervisor ($119,572) was requested but not funded in FY2024.

I found no FY2026 or FY2027 line that names tree care alone.

**Context on whether that money is enough.** The case file cites the City's FY2024 budget as reporting that it fulfilled 5% of street-tree pruning requests in FY2021 and 9% in FY2022. A draft City Auditor report from April 2023 says Forestry hasn't been able to adopt a proactive maintenance program. The case file says the FY2027 book replaces the pruning measures with trees planted, and that this isn't yet re-checked by a second reader.

For the exact tree contract amounts, the case file suggests requesting the tree-care contracts and invoices from FY2020 to now. The dataset's "Other Contractual Services" line is the likely home for contract work: $1,341,544 actual in FY2026, but it isn't broken out by trees.

For a specific street, I can pull the City's tree work orders for an address.

**Stump grinding:** Each removal has a matching stump-grinding order. - The dataset assigns each work order to one civic league, based on its primary street. Work on a street that borders two leagues could show up under only one.

results.q: What does the zoning ordinance say about short-term rentals in residential districts?
results.answer:
I found the short-term rental rules in Norfolk's Zoning Ordinance, but I couldn't read the full performance standard. That standard is in §4.2.3, and I only saw excerpts of it. The text I read is current through the PDF's cover date, October 13, 2026. The PDF is the authority.

**Definition.** The §4.2.3 excerpt defines a short-term rental unit (vacation rental) as a dwelling, or part of one, rented to a single-party guest for at least one night and fewer than 30 consecutive nights. That applies when all owners have their primary residence elsewhere. The same excerpt says a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) is required when the use is not registered under §4.2.3.F(10)(f). It lists other triggers, including one for the R-C district, but the excerpt cut off before the rest.

**Use table.** In the §3.2.12 residential use table, the row for "Short-term rental unit (vacation rental)" reads P/C, P/C, P/C, C, C, P/C, C across the residential districts. I couldn't see the column headings, so I can't tell you which district gets which letter.

The use-table case file says:
- "P/C" means the use is allowed, but a CUP may be required depending on the performance standards.
- "C" means a CUP is required.
- A blank means the use is prohibited.

**Registration and condos.** A §4.2.3 excerpt says that in a condominium or residential cooperative, the unit needs written permission from the association or board. That permission must go to the Department of City Planning before the use starts. The same excerpt describes optional registration for vacation rentals and homestays.

**Homestays.** A §4.3.3 excerpt covers homestays, which are an accessory use. It sets a maximum of two guests per bedroom offered, and no more than 10 guests in five bedrooms at one time. The operator stays liable for taxes. §2.3.6 exempts a registered homestay from the administrative review procedure.

**Short-Term Rental Limitation Overlay (§3.9.22).** This overlay, the [STRL-O](https\://norfolk.gov/DocumentCenter/View/35581/Adopted-Zoning-Ordinance#page=439), adds rules for vacation rentals in a concentrated residential area. Where it conflicts with the base zoning, the overlay governs. I don't know which addresses it covers. A parcel's overlay can be checked with the parcel inventory tool.
- Only two kinds of property can register. One is a property with an Active Zoning Approval (a CUP or Zoning Certificate) as of June 1, 2026. The other is a single-family or two-family property more than 300 linear feet from a vacation rental with an Active Zoning Approval.
- A property that meets the location rule but lacks the minimum off-street parking may operate only with a CUP.
- After the third violation in two years, the owner and operator get a certified-mail warning. After the fourth, a registered property is removed from the registry and is ineligible for two years.
- For a CUP property, the Zoning Administrator may recommend that City Council revoke the permit after the fourth violation. A revoked property may be ineligible for two years.

**Penalties (§7.6.1).** An excerpt of the Remedies section lists a civil penalty of $200 for the initial summons and $500 for each additional summons. These apply to running a short-term rental in violation of the ordinance or of a CUP condition.

**What I couldn't confirm.** I didn't read the full F(10)(e) and F(10)(f) standards, so I can't give the registration requirements, the parking minimums or the complete list of CUP triggers. Whether a given address qualifies depends on its district's column in the use table and on any overlay. A written Zoning Determination from City Planning is the binding answer (§2.3.8).

results.q: What's the plan for the old Military Circle Mall site?
results.answer:
I can't say that for sure, but here's what I found:

The records I can reach show a site still in preparation. I found no finished master plan for the former Military Circle Mall at 880 N. Military Highway.

**Money and studies so far**
- Council approved the transfer of the site from the Economic Development Authority on July 15, 2025, according to the case file's summary of the City's records.
- On August 25, 2026, Council approved a $200,000 advance to the Authority for site readiness studies, per [Ordinance No. 50487](https\://norfolkcityva.iqm2.com/Citizens/Detail_LegiFile.aspx?ID=5949). The City's letter says these studies are needed before the City can apply to the state's Business Ready Sites Program for infrastructure money.
- The [cooperation agreement](https\://NorfolkCityVA.iqm2.com/Citizens/FileOpen.aspx?Type=4&ID=25519) says the Authority has been awarded a $337,750 state grant, and the advance is to be repaid from it.
- The agreement lists the reports to be done: a site certification report, geotechnical, survey, environmental, cultural, species, wetland and traffic reviews, and an engineering report on water, sewer and roads. I found no copy of those reports yet.

**Demolition and timing**
- [WHRO reported on September 1, 2026](https\://www\.whro.org/local-government/2026-09-01/260901-militarycircle-saunders) that the City aimed to start demolition in October, and that the studies were expected to take six to eight months.
- [WTKR reported on September 29, 2026](https\://www\.wtkr.com/news/in-the-community/norfolk/norfolk-leaders-share-updates-on-casino-macarthur-mall-military-circle-mall-and-east-street-garage) that demolition was priced at nearly $3 million and the first phase would start the next month. WHRO reported that the $10 million demolition budget approved in 2023 would not grow.
- WTKR reported on September 4, 2026 that demolition was expected to take about 15 months.
- Per WHRO, the Deputy City Manager expected a master plan about a year after the studies conclude, and hoped incremental development with Sentara could begin within three years.
- I found no City record yet that demolition has begun.

**What isn't settled**
- **Ownership:** WHRO reported that Sentara owns the former J.C. Penney building and much of the parking inside the ring road.
- **Ross Dress for Less:** [WAVY reported on June 4, 2026](https\://www\.wavy.com/news/norfolk-moving-ahead-with-military-circle-mall-demo-without-ross-ok-citing-public-safety/amp/) that Ross effectively holds a veto inside the ring road, and had not consented as the City put demolition out to bid. WHRO reported in September that the City was still negotiating the Ross lease. [WTKR reported on July 14, 2026](https\://www\.wtkr.com/news/in-the-community/norfolk/multiple-bids-submitted-for-military-circle-demo-project-city-leader-reports) that breaking the lease could reportedly cost up to $16 million.
- **Capital plan:** The adopted FY 2027–2031 capital plan names no Military Circle project. [WHRO reported on May 20, 2026](https\://www\.whro.org/local-government/2026-05-20/052026-cipapproved-saunders) that the City chose the former Poplar Hall Elementary site for the East Side library and recreation center to avoid delays tied to Military Circle.

**Who decides:** Council approves agreements for the land. State law requires a public hearing before the City sells or leases it, with some exceptions, according to the case file.

What this might add up to: The records show the site is at the studies and lease-negotiation stage. Demolition is reported as planned, but the timing depends on the Ross lease and on Sentara's land, and no master plan is in place yet. The 2017 [Military Circle / Military Highway vision plan](https\://www\.norfolk.gov/DocumentCenter/View/27580/Military_Circle_UDA_Vision_Plan) describes a long-term goal of full high-density mixed-use redevelopment. That is a goal, not a current plan. For the terms of the City's deal with the Authority, the [cooperation agreement](https\://NorfolkCityVA.iqm2.com/Citizens/FileOpen.aspx?Type=4&ID=25519) is the record to read, and the City Council office can speak to the schedule.

results.q: How much does Norfolk budget for tree care?

results.q: What does the zoning ordinance say about short-term rentals in residential districts?
results.answer:
I found the short-term rental rules in the Zoning Ordinance, but the excerpts don't give the full residential-district standards, so this answer is incomplete.

**The definition and the permit trigger (§4.2.3).** The ordinance defines a short-term rental unit as a dwelling rented to a single-party guest for at least one night and fewer than 30 consecutive nights, when all owners have their primary residence elsewhere. §4.2.3, p. 507 says a Conditional Use Permit is required when the rental is not registered under §4.2.3.F(10)(f). The same excerpt lists further CUP triggers, including one for the R-C district, but the text is cut off before I could read them in full.

**Which residential districts allow it (§3.2.12).** The residential use table lists "Short-term rental unit (vacation rental)" with a mix of "P" (permitted) and "C" (Conditional Use Permit) entries across the district columns. §3.2.12, p. 201 The excerpt doesn't show which column is which district, so I can't say from it whether a given residential district needs a CUP.

**The overlay (§3.9.22).** The Short-Term Rental Limitation Overlay exists "to reduce the adverse effects resulting from the proliferation of short-term rental units in a concentrated, residential area." [§3.9.22, p. 439](https\://norfolk.gov/DocumentCenter/View/35581/Adopted-Zoning-Ordinance#page=439) The same section says the overlay governs where it conflicts with the base zoning. Under it, I found these registration eligibility rules:
- Properties with an active zoning approval (a CUP or Zoning Certificate for the use) as of June 1, 2026.
- Single-family or two-family homes more than 300 linear feet from a short-term rental with an active approval.

Properties that don't meet all off-street parking requirements can operate only with a CUP. §3.9.22, p. 440

**Penalties in the overlay.** For registered units, each violation must be documented. After a third violation in two years, the operator and owner get a certified-mail notice; a fourth violation removes the property from the registry for two years. For CUP units, a third violation brings a notice that the next violation may lead to a recommendation for revocation, and a fourth may lead to one. [§3.9.22, pp. 439–440](https\://norfolk.gov/DocumentCenter/View/35581/Adopted-Zoning-Ordinance#page=439)

**Registration and review.** §2.3.6 exempts a registered short-term rental (homestay) from the usual administrative review steps.

**What I didn't reach.** I didn't read the full §4.2.3.F(10) standards, including the registration requirements in (e) and (f) and the R-C and other district triggers. I also didn't check which parcels sit inside the overlay. The ordinance says the PDF is the authority, and the text I read is current through October 13, 2026.

If you give me an address, I can check whether its parcel is in the overlay. I can also try again to read the full §4.2.3.F(10) text.

results.q: What does the zoning ordinance say about short-term rentals in residential districts?
results.answer:
I found the short-term rental rules spread across several sections of Norfolk's Zoning Ordinance. I could not read the full registration and performance standards, so this answer is partial. The text I read is current through October 13, 2026, per the [ordinance PDF](https\://norfolk.gov/DocumentCenter/View/35581/Adopted-Zoning-Ordinance).

**Definition (§4.2.3).** The Performance Standards section defines a short-term rental unit as a dwelling, or part of one, rented to a single-party guest for at least one night and fewer than 30 consecutive nights, where all owners have their primary residence elsewhere. A Conditional Use Permit is required when the use is not registered under §4.2.3.F(10)(f). The rest of that list was cut off in my reading.

**Base residential districts (§3.2.12).** In the residential use table, I found "Short-term rental unit (vacation rental)" marked P/C in some district columns and C in others. In that table, P means permitted by right and C means a Conditional Use Permit. I did not match each column to its district, so I can't say which residential districts allow it by right.

**Short-Term Rental Limitation Overlay (§3.9.22).** The [overlay section](https\://norfolk.gov/DocumentCenter/View/35581/Adopted-Zoning-Ordinance#page=439) applies on top of the base district rules and controls where the two conflict. Its stated purpose is to reduce the adverse effects of many short-term rentals concentrated in one residential area. Under it:
- A property with an active zoning approval for a short-term rental as of June 1, 2026 can register to continue, and so can a single-family or two-family home more than 300 linear feet from an active short-term rental.
- A property that does not meet all minimum off-street parking requirements may operate only under a Conditional Use Permit.
- For registered rentals, the third violation in a two-year period triggers notice by certified mail, and the fourth removes the property from the registry for two years.
- For CUP rentals, the third violation can lead to a notice that the next one may bring a recommendation to City Council for revocation.

**Registration (§2.3.6).** The Administrative Review section exempts a residential dwelling registered under §4.2.3.F(10)(e) from its procedural steps.

**What I did not get:**
- The full text of §4.2.3.F(10)(e) and (f), so I can't give the registration requirements, the full list of CUP triggers, or the performance standards for registered rentals.
- Which properties sit inside the overlay. I read the overlay's rules but did not check any address against its boundaries. For a specific address, the parcel's zoning and overlays are the place to check.

For the binding answer on a specific property or use, the City's Zoning Determination from City Planning is the authority. The PDF linked above is also the authoritative text.

results.answer:
I found 810 Union St in Ward 4, on the 800 block of Union Street. The agenda records describe this address as City Hall. Two items approve a lease for "Space Within Norfolk City Hall, Located at 810 Union Street, for an ATM," with Truist Bank. Some of what follows may be City Hall activity rather than home-related. I can't tell from these records whether a home sits on this parcel.

**Street work right now**
- Lane and sidewalk closure, permit 26-3537, scheduled Sept. 14 to Dec. 31, 2026.
- Communications cable install (aerial and underground), permit 26-3536, scheduled Sept. 14 to Dec. 31, 2026.
- Lane and shoulder closure, permit 26-4041, scheduled Oct. 20 to Nov. 20, 2026. That end date is today.
- Earlier this fall, I found a lane and shoulder closure (26-3483, ended Oct. 14) and several oversize hauling permits, the latest 26-4265 (Nov. 4 to 11).

**Open city work orders**
These match on the street in Ward 4, not the house number, so they may not be at 810.
- Damaged tree removal, opened June 9, 2023, status: New Work Order.
- Limb or tree down removal, opened Feb. 12, 2026, status: New Work Order.
- Forestry general maintenance inspection, opened Nov. 13, 2026, status: On-Going.

**Complaints on this parcel (4, all closed)**
- Wetlands complaint, May 18, 2026, closed "Completed w/Notes" (City Planning).
- Trash and debris, May 13, 2026, closed "Unfounded" (Neighborhood Services).
- Outdoor storage/debris, May 27, 2025, closed (City Planning).
- Trash and debris, June 11, 2024, closed (Neighborhood Services).

I found no violations on this parcel.

**Permits and reviews**
- I found 178 permits on this parcel. Of the 10 most recent, most are Abandoned or Cancelled. Electrical permit E26-02256 is Issued (Aug. 13, 2026).
- I found 86 plan reviews. Most of the 10 shown are Approved (2024 to 2025). Plan review ZP25-00384 is Pending, with a due date of July 31, 2025.
- I found 2,733 inspection records. The 10 shown all have status Pending.

**Other facts from the parcel record**
- Trash pickup: Mon, Wed, Fri. Street sweeping: daily. Evacuation zone: A.
- Schools: PB Young and Ruffner Academy (elementary and middle), Booker T. Washington High.
- Nearest park: Town Point Park. Nearest library: Slover.

**Council and other elected officials**
Ward 4 Council: John E. "JP" Paige. Superward 7: Carlos J. Clanton. Virginia House District 92, Virginia Senate: Angelia Williams Graves, U.S. House: Robert C. Scott. Phone numbers are in the contacts below.

**Agenda items**
The two Truist Bank lease ordinances name 810 Union St:
- Ordinance No. 49637, City Council, June 25, 2024.
- Ordinance No. 49934, City Council, April 29, 2025.

I found no agenda items for other addresses on the 800 block.
